AMF-GRSP-SOM-C interactions were the main driving forces for the recovery of soil structure, and that the effects of HMs on AMF growth, soil properties and aggregate formation and stability were depth dependent.
AMF and its GRSP are important factors in improving soil aggregate stability and soil fertility in HM-polluted soils.
GRSP, AMF and SOM play an essential role in the formation of soil aggregates and the improvement of soil structure in Pb and Zn contaminated soils.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the introduction of AMF can be used to improve soil quality and aggregate formation in HM-polluted soils.
the effects of HM contamination on soil properties and aggregate stability could be significantly alleviated by AMF inoculation.

the effects of AMF on soil properties, aggregate formation and particle size distribution were closely related to the soil depths, and that the effects of Pb on AMF status were more serious than those of Zn in HM polluted soils.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the application of AMF can improve soil aggregate stability and SOM content in HM polluted soils.

the introduction of plant associated with AM fungi might be a successful biological tool for assisting the recovery of HM contaminated soils, and that appropriate management practices need to be developed to guarantee the maximum benefits from plant-mycorrhizal symbiosis during ecological recovery.
